routes.description: Establish that consciousness, intentionality, agency, and personal identity cannot be exhausted by physical descriptions, then identify a single nonphysical subject capable of persisting independently of its present body and entering later embodiment.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the mental features and identity conditions require a nonphysical bearer, bodily dependence is compatible with that bearer's continued existence, and a coherent mechanism or argument supports survival beyond bodily death.

motionBridge.description: Show that a conscious person includes one nonphysical subject whose identity can continue after the present organism dies.

centralBridges.description: Establish that phenomenal character or intrinsic intentionality is not captured by an exclusively physical inventory.
Connect irreducible mental properties to a single subject that bears and unifies the person's mental states.
Supply identity conditions under which that subject can remain the same person across bodily discontinuity or renewed embodiment.
Explain why dependence of embodied capacities on the brain does not entail destruction of the subject when the brain ceases functioning.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use reason-responsive agency or freedom to reinforce the distinction between mentality and bottom-up physical causation.
Provide cosmological or probabilistic support for recurrence or another opportunity for postmortem embodiment.

routes.description: Account for consciousness, intentionality, agency, and personal unity as properties or activities of natural organisms at appropriate explanatory scales, while challenging any inference from mental distinctiveness to a separable enduring substance.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic organism-level explanations accommodate the cited mental phenomena, brain dependence undermines an independently functioning bearer, and the proposed identity or cosmological grounds for postmortem survival are not required.

motionBridge.description: Show that the conscious person is a natural organism and that no independently surviving nonphysical subject is needed.

centralBridges.description: Explain mental properties at the organismic scale without reducing them to microphysical vocabulary or adding another substance.
Give physicalist-compatible accounts of phenomenal knowledge, intentional attitudes, and unified consciousness.
Use the systematic dependence of mental capacities on brain states and integrity to oppose separable personal existence.
Challenge the identity conditions and cosmological premises offered to support recurrence or postmortem persistence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve deliberation and reason-responsive action through compatibilist or higher-scale causal explanation.
Relate the onset and loss of conscious capacities to the presence of suitable neural organization.

sections.title: Phenomenal consciousness and physical explanation
sections.rationale: The status of qualia and phenomenal knowledge determines whether first-person experience supplies evidence for facts or properties beyond a natural physical account.

sections.title: Intentionality, mental causation, and agency
sections.rationale: Competing accounts of aboutness, reason-responsive action, and higher-level causation test whether mental activity requires a nonphysical source or fits an organismic framework.

sections.title: From nonphysical properties to subjects and personal identity
sections.rationale: The motion concerns substances rather than merely unusual properties, making the inference to a unified subject and its criteria of persistence an indispensable burden.

sections.title: Cosmology, recurrence, and postmortem survival
sections.rationale: The temporal probability argument, recurrence mechanism, and rival cosmological models bear on whether personal existence can recur after bodily death.

sections.title: Brain dependence, embodiment, and disembodied capacity
sections.rationale: Evidence concerning brain impairment, suitable neural conditions, and the capacities of a disembodied subject bears directly on separability and survival.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Qualia resist physical reduction because their felt first-person character is itself the phenomenon requiring explanation, unlike the mental effects of externally reduced phenomena such as heat.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Mary gains propositional knowledge of a determinate qualitative property, not merely an ability, because seeing red rules out alternative ways that the experience could have felt.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: Qualia and intentionality support property dualism, while the problem of personal identity provides the further route from nonphysical properties to substance dualism.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Tree rings have no intrinsic aboutness; they function as evidence only because observers interpret them through mental states that represent the tree's age.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: If time is infinite in both directions and each person lives only once, the probability of being alive now is zero; therefore reincarnation occurs or the infinite-past assumption is false.

chunk-004:c004-01.proposition: Blind bottom-up physical causes cannot ground free will because they do not respond to reasons, whereas causation by a higher-level mental subject can make conduct reason-responsive.

chunk-004:c004-05.proposition: Reincarnation need not depend on eternal recurrence or qualitative duplication, because unknown conditions might instead cause an enduring soul to enter another living organism.

chunk-004:c004-06.proposition: A soul is the single subject bearing all of a person's rational thoughts, sensations, and emotions, rather than an additional rational entity distinct from the ordinary subject of experience.

chunk-004:c004-09.proposition: Souls have always existed rather than emerging through evolution, but a soul can inhabit an organism only when suitable physical conditions, such as a brain capable of supporting intelligence, arise.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: A disembodied soul may survive bodily death while being unable to think or act, because brain damage impairs human capacities and death destroys the entire brain that supports them.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Mary's acquisition of experiential knowledge is compatible with identity theory because fully knowing certain physical brain states may require occupying those states.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Reality contains scale-specific properties that cannot be defined from lower-scale properties, without making the lower scale metaphysically privileged or abandoning naturalism.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Functionalist accounts can explain intentional attitudes within identity theory, making intentionality less troublesome for physicalism than consciousness or qualia.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Macroscopic indeterminacy does not yield libertarian freedom, while action from normally acquired beliefs and desires without defeating interference supplies sufficient compatibilist freedom.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Emergent or downward-causal organization does not establish substance dualism because higher-scale events remain events occurring in the brain, without an additional mental substance.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: Contemporary cosmology makes a finite past and infinite future more plausible than an infinite past, while expansion and entropy considerations also undermine cosmic recurrence.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Standard projections of an eternally expanding universe imply eventual proton and black-hole decay followed only by sparse radiation, so stars, people, and recurrent conditions never return.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: A resemblance-based account of personal identity does not readily support reincarnation as an animal because an animal would not be a qualitative duplicate of the person.

chunk-005:chunk005-candidate-01.proposition: Pervasive impairment from brain damage supports the conclusion that human capacities depend on the brain rather than an independently functioning soul.

chunk-005:chunk005-candidate-05.proposition: Evidence linking relevant mental states to brain activity makes it reasonable to deny that a soul is attached to a fetus before the requisite neural activity develops.
